AUTHOR: Beyan
TITLE: Extracting statistically significant behaviour from fish tracking data with and without large dataset cleaning
REGION: Kenting National Park (nuclear power plant intake bay), Taiwan
DATA: Fish4Knowledge project raw observatory archive: 12,247 ten-minute videos from fixed camera at 2 m, with per-video water temperature; 3,649,007 trajectories
V_EV: Sec. 3: 'The camera used in this study was at a depth of 2 m ... the scene is greatly affected by illumination variations'
D2: no train/test split (unsupervised mcRBM clustering; evaluation on random manually examined subset)
R_EV: Sec. 3: 'The videos were captured from one of four fixed cameras ... in the intake bay of the third nuclear power plant inside Kenting National Park'
C_EV: Sec. 3: '1000 of the 3.6 million fish trajectories were manually examined ... These 1000 trajectories led to 16,504 detections, of which 16,210 were actually fish'
E_EV: Sec. 6: 'this work presents reliable evidence for an increase in fish speed as water temperature increases'; 'we had no ground truth to validate the correctness of the estimated speeds'
ARCH: F4K covariance-based tracker + BGOT decision-tree species classifier; B-spline trajectory features + mean-covariance RBM clustering for outlier (erroneous trajectory) removal
METR: % valid trajectories from manual sample, agreement of outlier detection with manual labels, Kruskal-Wallis/Tukey-Kramer/Mann-Kendall tests on speed vs temperature
NOTE: Uses the full Fish4Knowledge observatory archive (12,247 videos, deployment info + water temperature), not the F4K benchmark recognition/FCS collections -> included; verifier should confirm against the benchmark-only rule. Detection/tracking/recognition outputs come from earlier F4K systems; this paper's ML component is unsupervised mcRBM outlier detection, so no train/test split (D NR). C5 = manual FP verification of 1000 random trajectories (2% FP detections, 25.5% erroneous trajectories) plus explicit removal of incorrect trajectory assignments; outlier rule uses a cluster-cardinality threshold (A=10% of median, clusters <975 trajectories) which was not treated as a score threshold (C1=NR, low confidence; if counted, C_ALL would be Y). Outlier detector agreement with manual labels: 52% of erroneous detected, 78% of correct kept. Speed vs temperature: Mann-Kendall trend p<0.05 (not hierarchical model).
